docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Item LDM is the standard, governed logical interface for eBay item-domain data, abstracting fragmented underlying physical sources to enable self-service consumption on GDS platform to support business use cases such as data engineering, analytics, and ML feature engineering.

docs.title: Core Concepts
docs.text:
Understanding Item domain fundamentals:

  • Item, Variation, Product

    Core entity hierarchy: listings (item), SKUs (variation), and catalog references (product/ePID)

  • Attributes vs Aspects

    Two ways to describe items: seller-provided attributes vs SAP-processed aspects with higher quality

  • Variation Traits

    SKU-level differentiators like Color, Size, Network that distinguish variations

SELECT item_id, variation_id, variation_sku, variation_price
FROM gds.variation

Use case: Brand, material, color (EAV pattern)

WHERE m.attr_id = 1000;

SELECT item_id, transaction_id, transaction_date, transaction_amount

docs.title: How to Query Relationships
docs.text:
1. For 1:N / N:1 Relationships

    v.variation_sku,
    v.variation_price
FROM gds.variation v
WHERE v.item_id = 123456789;

docs.text: Understanding the foundational concepts in the Item domain.

docs.title: Item
docs.text:
Item

Definition: A listing on eBay's platform. In the data warehouse, item_id (also known as listing_id) uniquely identifies each item.

Characteristics:

  • Can be single-SKU (SSKU) or multi-SKU (MSKU)
  • Contains seller-provided metadata (title, price, description, category)
  • Has attributes (seller input) and aspects (SAP-generated)

Example:

"Apple iPhone 17 Pro (Unlocked, AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile) New Open Box, Never Used"

  • Item ID: 227255267188
  • Price: $1,129.99
  • Attributes: Brand=Apple, Condition=Open Box, Storage=256GB, Network=Unlocked
  • Aspects: Screen Size=6.3", Operating System=iOS, Camera Resolution=48MP

docs.title: Variation
docs.text:
Variation

Definition: A specific SKU within a multi-variation listing, reflecting different product configurations.

Characteristics:

  • Only exists for MSKU items
  • Has variation traits (characteristics that differ across SKUs)
  • Each variation has its own price, quantity, SKU

Example:

For the iPhone listing above, variations might include:

  • Variation 1: Network=AT&T, Storage=256GB, Color=Blue
  • Variation 2: Network=T-Mobile, Storage=512GB, Color=Silver
  • Variation 3: Network=Verizon, Storage=1TB, Color=Orange

Variation Traits: Network, Storage Capacity, Color

docs.title: Product
docs.text:
Product

Definition: Product catalog reference (ePID - eBay Product ID) that groups items representing the same physical entity.

Types:

  • Seller-tagged (PROD_REF_ID): Seller manually assigns ePID during listing creation
  • Auto-tagged (AT_PROD_REF_ID): eBay's Structured Data Adoption team assigns ePID

Relationship:

  • Multiple items (different sellers, conditions, prices) → Same product (ePID)
  • Enables cross-listing analysis and product catalog mapping

Example:

ePID 285507661 = "iPhone 15 Pro" → Links all iPhone 15 Pro listings regardless of seller

docs.title: Entity Relationships
docs.text:
• One item can have 0 to many variations (1:N)
  • Multiple items reference the same product via ePID (N:1)

docs.title: Attributes vs Aspects
docs.text:
Two ways to describe item characteristics. The core difference lies in data source and quality:

Attribute vs Aspect Comparison

Dimension Attribute Aspect Data Source Seller input Processed from attributes by SAP (Search Annotation Platform) Data Quality Raw data, inconsistent format Cleaned, standardized, enriched Generation Seller provides when creating listing SAP extracts, normalizes, and standardizes from attributes Primary Use View Item Page display, basic filtering Search indexing, recommendations, high-precision classification Visibility Buyer-facing (shown on product page) Internal eBay systems (search, recommendation) Example Brand=apple, Storage=256 GB, Color=dark blue Brand=Apple, Storage=256GB, Color=Blue, Screen_Size=6.3" Storage EAV pattern Structured taxonomy with namespace/classifier IDs Tables dw_attr_detail_values, dw_attr_lstg_dtl, dw_attr_shpmt_dtl item_aspct_clssfctn_sap, vrtn_aspct_clssfctn_sap

Why do we need Aspects?

Seller-provided attributes have inconsistent quality (typos, format variations, missing information), which cannot meet the precision requirements of search and recommendation systems. SAP generates high-quality aspects through:

  • Normalization: apple → Apple, 256 GB → 256GB (via UNS - Unified Normalization Service)
  • Enrichment: Extract missing attributes from title/description (e.g., Screen Size, OS)
  • Standardization: Map to unified names/values using UMS (Unified Metadata System)

Real-world Example

Seller-provided Attributes: 

Brand=apple, Storage=256 GB, Color=dark blue

SAP-generated Aspects: 

Brand=Apple, Storage=256GB, Color=Blue, 
Screen_Size=6.3", Operating_System=iOS, Camera_Resolution=48MP

Notice how aspects are standardized and include additional information extracted from the listing.

docs.title: Variation Traits
docs.text:
Traits

Definition: Variation-level characteristics that differentiate SKUs within the same multi-SKU item.

Characteristics:

  • Only exist for MSKU items with variations
  • Describe the specific features that differ across variations
  • Common trait types: Color, Size, Style, Capacity, Network, Material

Purpose:

  • Enable SKU differentiation within the same listing
  • Support variation-level analysis (e.g., which color/size sells better)
  • Help buyers select the specific variant they want

Examples:

For a clothing item with multiple variations:

  • Traits: Color (Red, Blue, Black), Size (S, M, L, XL)
  • Variation 1: Color=Red, Size=S
  • Variation 2: Color=Blue, Size=M
  • Variation 3: Color=Black, Size=L

For a smartphone listing:

  • Traits: Network (AT&T, Verizon, Unlocked), Storage (128GB, 256GB, 512GB), Color (Blue, Silver, Gold)
  • Variation 1: Network=AT&T, Storage=256GB, Color=Blue
  • Variation 2: Network=Unlocked, Storage=512GB, Color=Silver

Key Distinction:

  • Attributes/Aspects describe the item as a whole (e.g., Brand=Apple applies to all variations)
  • Traits describe differences between variations (e.g., Color=Blue vs Color=Silver)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
LDM Name: item

Description: The core listing entity representing an item/product listing on the platform. Contains comprehensive information about items including title, pricing, category, seller, and listing lifecycle.

Primary Key: item_id

Relationship Type: Base Entity (can be queried independently)

docs.title: Identifiers
docs.text:
• item_id - Unique item identifier (Primary Key)
  • item_site_id - Site ID (0=US, 3=UK, 15=Australia, etc.)
  • seller_id - Seller user ID

docs.title: Item Information
docs.text:
• item_title - Item title/name
  • item_subtitle - Item subtitle (optional)
  • item_price - Current item price
  • item_quantity - Available quantity
  • item_cndtn_id - Item condition ID
  • 1000 = New
  • 3000 = Used
  • 1500 = New other
  • 2000 = Manufacturer refurbished

docs.title: Category & Classification
docs.text:
• leaf_categ_id - Leaf category ID
  • meta_categ_id - Meta category ID
  • l1_categ_id - Level 1 category ID
  • l2_categ_id - Level 2 category ID

docs.title: Listing Lifecycle
docs.text:
• item_start_dt - Listing start date/time
  • item_end_dt - Listing end date/time
  • listing_type - Listing format (Auction, Fixed Price, etc.)
  • listing_status - Current status (Active, Ended, etc.)

docs.title: Product Reference
docs.text: • prod_ref_id - Product reference ID (ePID) - Links to Product catalog

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
• view_count - Number of views
  • watch_count - Number of watchers
  • sold_quantity - Quantity sold

docs.title: Additional Attributes
docs.text:
• shipping_type - Shipping method
  • returns_accepted - Whether returns are accepted
  • item_location - Item location (city, state, country)
  • Plus 80+ additional fields...

Note: The complete field list contains 100+ fields. Contact the GDS team for the full schema definition.

docs.title: Basic Item Query
docs.text:
-- Get items in a specific category
SELECT 
    item_id,
    item_title,
    item_price,
    item_quantity,
    seller_id,
    item_cndtn_id
FROM item
WHERE item_site_id = 0
  AND leaf_categ_id = 58058  -- Cell Phones & Accessories
  AND item_cndtn_id = 1000   -- New condition
LIMIT 100;

docs.title: Filter by Price Range
docs.text:
-- Find items within price range
SELECT 
    item_id,
    item_title,
    item_price,
    item_start_dt
FROM item
WHERE item_site_id = 0
  AND leaf_categ_id = 58058
  AND item_price BETWEEN 100 AND 500
  AND item_quantity > 0
ORDER BY item_price ASC
LIMIT 100;

docs.title: Recently Listed Items
docs.text:
-- Get recently listed items
SELECT 
    item_id,
    item_title,
    item_price,
    item_start_dt,
    seller_id
FROM item
WHERE item_site_id = 0
  AND leaf_categ_id = 58058
  AND item_start_dt >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '7' DAY
ORDER BY item_start_dt DESC
LIMIT 100;

docs.title: Join with Product Catalog
docs.text:
-- Items with product catalog information
SELECT 
    i.item_id,
    i.item_title,
    i.item_price,
    p.prod_ref_id,
    p.product_name,
    p.product_brand
FROM item i
LEFT JOIN product p ON i.prod_ref_id = p.prod_ref_id
WHERE i.item_site_id = 0
  AND i.leaf_categ_id = 58058
LIMIT 100;

docs.text:

docs.title: Always Use Partition Filters
docs.text:
Item tables are partitioned by item_site_id. Always include this in your WHERE clause:

-- Good
WHERE item_site_id = 0  -- Filters to single partition

-- Bad
WHERE item_title LIKE '%iPhone%'  -- Scans all partitions

docs.title: Limit Result Sets
docs.text:
Use LIMIT for exploratory queries:

SELECT * FROM item
WHERE item_site_id = 0
LIMIT 100;  -- Prevents scanning millions of rows

docs.title: Select Specific Columns
docs.text:
Avoid SELECT * - only select columns you need:

-- Good
SELECT item_id, item_title, item_price
FROM item;

-- Bad
SELECT *  -- Returns 100+ columns
FROM item;

docs.title: Migration Guide
docs.text: How to migrate from legacy Hive tables to Item Domain LDM.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Item Domain LDM consolidates 30+ fragmented Hive tables into unified logical entities. This guide helps you migrate existing queries to the new LDM interface.

Benefits of migrating:

  • Simpler queries: Query by business concepts instead of physical table names
  • Better performance: Optimized materialized views on DLS
  • Unified interface: Consistent access pattern across all item-related data
  • Governed data: Standardized, quality-controlled data models

docs.title: Step 1: Identify Your Legacy Table
docs.text:
Find your current table in the mapping below:

Legacy Table LDM Entity Migration Complexity DW_LSTG_ITEM gds.item Low - Direct mapping LSTG_ITEM_VRTN gds.variation Low - Direct mapping DW_LSTG_ITEM_PROD_REF gds.product Low - Join with item DW_ATTR_DETAIL_VALUES gds.dw_attr_detail_values Low - Direct mapping DW_ATTR_LSTG_DTL gds.dw_attr_lstg_dtl Low - Direct mapping ITEM_ASPCT_CLSSFCTN_SAP gds.item_aspct_clssfctn_sap Low - Direct mapping

docs.title: Step 2: Update Your Query
docs.text: Replace the table name and schema. Most queries require minimal changes.

docs.title: Step 3: Test and Validate
docs.text: Compare results between legacy and LDM queries to ensure correctness.

docs.title: Scenario 1: Basic Item Query
docs.text:

    item_id,
    item_title,
    item_price,
    leaf_categ_id,
    seller_id,
    item_site_id
FROM DW_LSTG_ITEM
WHERE item_site_id = 0
  AND leaf_categ_id = 58058
  AND auct_end_dt >= CURRENT_DATE
LIMIT 100;

SELECT 
    item_id,
    item_title,
    item_price,
    leaf_categ_id,
    seller_id,
    item_site_id
FROM gds.item
WHERE item_site_id = 0
  AND leaf_categ_id = 58058
  AND auct_end_dt >= CURRENT_DATE
LIMIT 100;

Changes: - ✅ Replace DW_LSTG_ITEM → gds.item - ✅ Column names remain the same - ✅ WHERE clause unchanged

    i.item_title,
    p.prod_ref_id,
    p.at_prod_ref_id

WHERE i.item_site_id = 0
  AND p.prod_ref_id IS NOT NULL

docs.title: Migration Checklist
docs.text:
Before migrating your queries:

  • Identify all legacy tables used in your current queries
  • Map each legacy table to its corresponding LDM entity
  • Update table references from legacy to gds.* schema
  • Test queries in development environment
  • Validate results match legacy query output
  • Update downstream dependencies (dashboards, reports, pipelines)
  • Document migration for your team

docs.title: Example 1: Basic Item Query
docs.text:
Get basic information for items in a specific category:

SELECT 
    item_id,
    item_title,
    item_price,
    item_quantity,
    seller_id
FROM gds.item
WHERE item_site_id = 0           -- US site
  AND item_cndtn_id = 1000       -- New condition
LIMIT 100;

docs.title: Modeling Strategy
docs.text: This document explains the unified strategy for identifying entities, attributes, and relationships in Logical Data Model Design.

docs.title: 1. Entity
docs.text: A business object that satisfies the following identification principles:

docs.title: Principle 1: Unique Identifier
docs.text: Has unique identifier that represents individual instance.

docs.title: Principle 2: Independent Lifecycle
docs.text: Can be created, updated, or deleted independently of other entities.

docs.title: Principle 3: Referenced by Multiple Entities
docs.text:
Participates in relationships with multiple entities.

Examples: - ✅ Item - has item_id, independent lifecycle, relates to Variation/Product/Deal - ✅ Product - has product_id (ePID), exists independently, referenced by multiple items - ✅ Trait - individual instance referenced by multiple entities

docs.title: 2. Entity Attribute
docs.text:
A property that belongs to and describes a single entity. It has no independent existence outside the entity.

Examples: - item_title - describes Item

docs.title: 3. Relationship
docs.text: A connection between two or more entities. Relationships can be one-to-many (1:N), many-to-one (N:1), or many-to-many (M:N).

docs.title: 1:N (One-to-Many) / N:1 (Many-to-One)
docs.text:
One entity instance can be associated with multiple instances of another entity. Foreign key resides in the "many" side.

Example: Item → Variation 

Item (1) ─────< Variation (N)

One item has multiple variations

docs.title: M:N (Many-to-Many)
docs.text:
Multiple instances on both sides can be associated with each other.

Example: Item ↔ Attribute 

Item (M) >─────< Attribute (N)

An Item can have multiple Attributes
An Attribute can be used by multiple Items

docs.title: 4. Relationship Attribute
docs.text:
A property that belongs to the relationship between two entities, not to either entity alone. It describes the connection, not the entities themselves.

Examples: - photo_count - in Item ↔ Trait mapping, describes how many photos this item has for this trait

docs.title: Step 2: LDM Definition
docs.text: Based on Step 1 identification, define logical data models:

docs.title: Entity → LDM
docs.text:
• Create dedicated LDM for each entity
  • Primary key: entity's unique identifier
  • Fields: entity attributes

docs.title: Relationship → LDM Structure
docs.text:
• 1:N / N:1: Foreign key in the "many" side's LDM
  • M:N:
  • Long-term vision: Query entity LDMs directly, system auto-materializes joins
  • Short-term approach: Create mapping LDM (see Step 3 for details)

docs.title: Step 3: Physical Source Mapping
docs.text: Map physical Hive tables to LDMs based on table granularity and type.

docs.title: 1. Granularity Analysis
docs.text:
Analyze physical table primary key structure to determine granularity:

  • Single entity key (e.g., item_id) → Entity table
  • Composite key with two entity FKs (e.g., item_id + attr_id) → Relationship table (M:N)
  • Composite key with entity FK + dimensions (e.g., item_id + snapshot_date) → Historical/SCD table
  • Aggregated dimensions (e.g., category_id + date) → Summary table

docs.title: Entity Tables → Entity LDM
docs.text:
Physical tables with entity-level granularity map to entity LDMs.

  • Single source: One physical table → One LDM (e.g., CTLG_PROD_FACT → product)
  • Multi-source: Multiple physical tables → One LDM (e.g., 11 tables → item)
  • Principle: One field has one source table (for given update frequency)
  • Merge complementary attributes from different sources

docs.title: Relationship Tables → Mapping LDM (M:N)
docs.text:
Short-term Approach: Physical M:N tables map directly to mapping LDMs with pre-denormalized attributes.

Mapping LDMs include not just foreign keys, but also denormalized entity attributes and relationship attributes.

Example: dw_attr_detail_values (physical table) → dw_attr_detail_values (mapping LDM) 

-- Physical table structure
item_id, attr_id, value_id, attr_name, value_desc

-- Maps to: Item (M) ↔ Attribute (N)
-- Denormalized: attr_name, value_desc
-- Relationship attributes: none in this case

Benefits: Faster queries, simpler SQL (2-table join instead of 3-table join)

docs.title: SCD2 Tables → Entity/Relationship LDM with Temporal Filtering
docs.text:
Physical SCD2 tables track historical changes over time.

Mapping approach: - Map to corresponding entity or relationship LDM - Add temporal filtering logic in queries

Example: DW_PES_ELGBLT_HIST → dw_pes_elgblt_hist (Item ↔ Business Program mapping) 

-- Current state query
WHERE eff_end_dt IS NULL

-- Point-in-time query  
WHERE snapshot_date BETWEEN eff_start_dt AND eff_end_dt

docs.title: Summary Tables → Typically Not Modeled
docs.text:
Aggregated summary tables contain pre-computed metrics and typically are not modeled as LDMs.

Rationale: - Different granularity (aggregated vs entity-level) - Pre-computed views, not source of truth - Query directly from physical table when needed

Example: CTLG_BRWS_NODE_SD (browse node summary by date) - used as-is, not abstracted into LDM

docs.title: 3. Long-term Vision: DDF Dynamic Materialization
docs.text:
In the future, the platform's Declarative Data Flow (DDF) capability will enable:

  • Dynamic Materialization: Automatically optimize M:N joins based on query patterns
  • Transparent Performance: No manual denormalization needed
  • Simplified Queries: Users query entity LDMs directly, system auto-generates mapping tables

Note: DDF is a long-term roadmap item. For now, use the pre-denormalized mapping LDMs provided.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Mapping LDM Name: dw_attr_detail_values

Description: Many-to-many relationship between Items and Attribute Values using the EAV (Entity-Attribute-Value) pattern for basic item attributes.

Primary Keys: item_id, attr_id, value_id

docs.title: Schema Structure
docs.text:
item_id        BIGINT      FK to Item
attr_id        BIGINT      Attribute identifier
attr_name      VARCHAR     Attribute name (denormalized)
value_id       BIGINT      Value identifier
value_desc     VARCHAR     Attribute value (denormalized)

docs.title: Get All Attributes for an Item
docs.text:
SELECT 
    item_id,
    attr_name,
    value_desc
FROM gds.item_attribute_mapping
WHERE item_id = 123456789;

docs.title: Filter by Specific Attribute
docs.text:
-- Get brand information for items
SELECT 
    item_id,
    attr_name,
    value_desc
FROM gds.item_attribute_mapping
WHERE item_id IN (123456789, 987654321)
  AND attr_name = 'Brand';

docs.title: Join with Item Entity
docs.text:
-- Get items with specific attribute value
SELECT 
    i.item_id,
    i.item_title,
    i.item_price,
    m.attr_name,
    m.value_desc
FROM gds.item i
JOIN gds.item_attribute_mapping m ON i.item_id = m.item_id
WHERE i.item_site_id = 0
  AND m.attr_name = 'Brand'
  AND m.value_desc = 'Apple'
LIMIT 100;

docs.title:
-- Get items matching multiple attribute criteria
SELECT 
    i.item_id,
    i.item_title,
    MAX(CASE WHEN m.attr_name = 'Brand' THEN m.value_desc END) AS brand,
    MAX(CASE WHEN m.attr_name = 'Model' THEN m.value_desc END) AS model,
    MAX(CASE WHEN m.attr_name = 'Color' THEN m.value_desc END) AS color
FROM gds.item i
JOIN gds.item_attribute_mapping m ON i.item_id = m.item_id
WHERE i.item_site_id = 0
  AND m.attr_name IN ('Brand', 'Model', 'Color')
GROUP BY i.item_id, i.item_title
HAVING MAX(CASE WHEN m.attr_name = 'Brand' THEN m.value_desc END) = 'Apple'
LIMIT 100;
